The honest starting point: Conair is not a high-speed brushless dryer. All three Canadian models we track are conventional 1875W designs that rely more on heat than on moving air. If drying speed or airflow is your priority, a Laifen, Dreame or Dyson will beat them.

What Conair does offer is real, though. The 318RC carries 9,491 ratings at 4.4★ in Canada, Conair has supported Canadian warranties for decades, and the brand holds roughly 17.9% of unit sales in the Canadian category — second only to slopehill. If you want the lowest-risk cheap dryer and you do not have thick or long hair, that combination is genuinely hard to beat.

Conair hair dryer models compared

Conair sells three hair dryers we track in Canada, and the differences between them are smaller than the price gaps suggest.

What we checked for every model:

  • CAD price and current Amazon.ca rating with rating count
  • Estimated monthly unit sales, and how long the listing has been live
  • Category BSR and whether the brand operates the listing
  • Who holds the Buy Box, because it determines who honours a warranty claim
  • Whether the design relies on heat or airflow, which decides who it suits

How to read the labels in this guide. Review analysis means a pattern across all 8,261 Canadian reviews in our dataset. Amazon.ca data is verifiable by you today. Buyer feedback is a single quoted experience. Manufacturer claim is unverified.

One honest caveat. Our review sample averages 3.37 stars while these products display 4.4–4.5 stars on Amazon.ca, because the export skews toward recent and critical reviews. We use it for theme and pain-point analysis only, never as a substitute for a product’s displayed rating.

1. Conair 318RC — the best value, and the volume leader

about C$25 · 4.4★ (9,491 ratings) · about 1,957 units/month · BSR #4 · 6.5 years on sale · Buy Box: Amazon (3 sellers)

What we liked

  • 9,491 ratings at 4.4★ — the third-largest review base of any model in our dataset, and a genuinely reassuring sample Amazon.ca data
  • about C$25 with roughly 1,957 units a month at BSR #4 — one of the highest-volume dryers in Canada Amazon.ca data
  • 6.5 years on sale, so this is not a new listing riding a launch spike Amazon.ca data

What we didn’t

Is Conair a reliable brand?

Conair has the longest service history in this category, and its models still sit in the price band where complaints are most common. Both things are true.

What the brand brings:

FactorAssessment
Canadian warranty supportDecades of history — the strongest of any brand we cover
Review base9,491 ratings on the 318RC alone, at 4.4★
DistributionCostco Canada, Walmart Canada, Canadian Tire, Best Buy — you can buy in person
Retail priceabout C$25 to about C$61 — the cheapest credible option
Motor technologyConventional 1875W, not high-speed brushless
Warranty counterpartyAmazon or a third party — no brand-operated listing

What the category data says about the price band:

Price bandReviewsAverage ratingComplaint rate
Under C$503,2593.39★30.3%
C$50–1208873.52★29.0%
Over C$1203344.43★9.6%

All three Conair models sit in the budget band. The 30.3% figure is not a criticism of Conair specifically — it describes the band, which every budget brand competes in. But it does mean a Conair carries roughly three times the complaint rate of a dryer over C$120 Review analysis.

The one structural gap. Unlike Laifen, Dreame and wavytalk — all of which operate brand-controlled Amazon.ca listings — Conair has no brand-operated storefront among the models we track. All three have Amazon or a third party holding the Buy Box with two or three competing sellers. Warranty and service complaints were the second-largest cluster in our dataset at 610 negative mentions and an 81% negative share, and reseller listings where nobody owns the claim are a large contributor Review analysis.

Where that leaves the recommendation. Conair is a good low-risk budget choice because of the service history and the enormous satisfied buyer base. It is not a performance choice, and the honest way to say it is that you are trading drying speed and airflow for price and support.

Three things to verify before buying any Conair:

  1. The ALCI plug — a rectangular GFCI-style box on the plug end. One Canadian reviewer flagged a dryer sold on Amazon.ca as non-compliant and recalled for missing it
  2. The seller — with two or three competing sellers, confirm who is shipping before relying on the warranty
  3. Whether you would be better off at about C$100. The InfinitiPro at about C$61 is only C$39 below the Laifen Air, which moves you into the price band where complaint rates drop to 9.6%. See our best hair dryers guide for that comparison

Conair hair dryer FAQ

Is Conair a good hair dryer brand? It depends what you want. Conair is not a high-speed brushless dryer, so if drying speed is your priority a Laifen or Dyson will beat it. What Conair offers is decades of Canadian warranty support and a very large satisfied buyer base — 9,491 ratings at 4.4 stars on the 318RC alone.

Which Conair hair dryer is best? The InfinitiPro FloMotion Pro at about C$61 is the most capable, with 1,079 ratings at 4.5 stars and around 1,081 units a month. The 318RC at about C$25 is the best value and the highest-volume Conair in Canada at roughly 1,957 units a month.

Does Conair make a high-speed brushless hair dryer? Not in the Canadian models we track. All three Conair listings in our dataset are conventional 1875W designs that rely more on heat than on airflow. That is a real limitation if your hair is thick or long, where airflow is what actually shortens drying time.

Is Conair sold by the brand on Amazon.ca? No. All three Conair listings in our dataset have Amazon or a third party holding the Buy Box, with two or three competing sellers. Unlike Laifen, Dreame and wavytalk, there is no brand-operated storefront here — so the warranty counterparty is less clear.

Why does Conair have such a low complaint rate in your data? It does not, and we want to be precise. Conair’s models sit in the under-C$50 and C$50–60 bands, where our data shows a 30.3% complaint rate across 3,259 reviews, against 9.6% for dryers over C$120. The high star ratings reflect that most buyers are satisfied, not that complaints are rare.

Is Conair a good choice for fine hair? Partly. It is a heat-first design, which is the opposite of what fine hair wants. But it does offer multiple heat settings and a cool shot at a very low price, and Conair has a genuine Canadian service history. See our fine hair guide for the trade-offs.

Our verdict on Conair hair dryers

Conair is a good low-risk budget choice and a poor performance choice. Both halves of that sentence matter.

Buy the 318RC at about C$25 if you want the lowest-risk cheap dryer in Canada. 9,491 ratings at 4.4★, 6.5 years on sale, roughly 1,957 units a month, and a brand that has supported Canadian warranties for decades. For occasional use on hair that is not especially thick, it is hard to argue with.

Buy the InfinitiPro FloMotion Pro at about C$61 if you want the diffuser and the most capable Conair. But be aware that at about C$61 you are only C$39 below the Laifen Air, which sits in the price band where complaint rates fall from 30.3% to 9.6%. That is a smaller gap than most buyers assume.

Do not buy Conair if your hair is thick or long. All three models are conventional heat-first designs, and our data shows airflow complaints run one way — reviewers never say a dryer is too powerful. See our thick hair guide for what to buy instead.

And check the ALCI plug and the cord strain relief on arrival, whichever you choose. Cord and connector failure accounted for 417 mentions in our dataset — see how long hair dryers actually last.
